About 5 to 7 years in security engineering, application security, or cloud security.
Hands-on experience securing LLM applications, agents, or AI developer tools, including prompt injection, data leakage, excessive agency, and insecure tool use.
Strong in non-human identity: OAuth, SSO, SCIM, service accounts, and secrets.
Writes and ships code, building the tooling instead of stopping at a recommendation.
Explains risk clearly to engineers and non-engineers, and can say yes with conditions.

Experience building evaluations or adversarial tests for AI systems.
Experience with AI gateways, SSPM, CASB, or DLP tools.

new_jobs.title: Senior Computer Vision Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Description

Fishers, IN, or nearby. This is an on-site position, not a remote one.

Company

At Arrive AI (Nasdaq: ARAI), we're not just building products; we're transforming the future of the Autonomous Last Mile™ (ALM). Over a decade ago, we started with a pioneering vision and patents for the first smart mailbox for drone delivery. Through systematic research, development, and deep customer collaboration, we've evolved to today, where we deploy Arrive Points: smart lockers and mini-cross-docks for frictionless drone, robotic, and courier delivery, from medical supplies to meals to e-commerce. Arrive AI is now scaling the ALM network and platform of the future for all autonomous delivery providers, services, and customers. We are the intelligent choice for the last inch of the Autonomous Last Mile™.

About Us

We move fast, balancing strategy with opportunity. We are merit-based, valuing integrity, innovation, and treating others as we want to be treated. At Arrive AI, every employee is an equity holder and a business owner. Our shared vision, ownership, and culture fuel our mission to revolutionize autonomous delivery.

Product Team

You'll be joining Arrive AI's Product Team to revolutionize Autonomous Last Mile (ALM) logistics by transforming over a decade of research, design, and customer collaboration into the world's first autonomous logistics network and platform. Our fast-paced skunkworks team rapidly iterates, prototypes, and develops next-generation Arrive Point units, networks, and AI-powered platforms. By integrating hardware, robotics, IoT, software, data, AI, and manufacturing, we're driving a bold roadmap for ALM innovation. Based in Fishers, IN, we offer a unique opportunity to do your life's best work, shape the future, and share in the success.

The Role

We're seeking a Senior Computer Vision Engineer to own the Arrive Point vision pipeline end-to-end: from the camera, through inference on the edge device, to the events that ArriveOS acts on and the data that reaches the cloud. You'll decide which models we run, train and optimize them, deploy them to NVIDIA Jetson hardware, and keep them accurate in the field.

This is a hands-on senior role with a bias toward the edge device. You'll work directly in C++ and Python with NVIDIA's DeepStream, GStreamer, Triton Inference Server, TensorRT, and related frameworks. You'll be familiar with the cloud side and work closely with our platform team, who manages our operating system and cloud services.

What You'll Do

Own the vision pipeline: Own the Arrive Point vision stack from camera ingress through inference to the events ArriveOS consumes and the data that reaches the cloud.
Build edge pipelines: Develop and maintain C++ pipelines with NVIDIA's DeepStream and GStreamer on Jetson Orin and Thor, using Triton Inference Server and TensorRT.
Select and train models: Evaluate, select, train, and fine-tune the right model for each task, from binary classifiers and CNNs to vision transformers, object detectors, and vision-language models.
Optimize for the edge: Export models through ONNX to TensorRT, build per-platform engines (FP16, INT8), and verify accuracy, latency, and memory on the device.
Collect data on real hardware: Sample, curate, and label data from deployed cameras, fine-tune their configurations, and address edge cases.
Run the model lifecycle: Maintain the training and release pipeline, including dataset versioning, CI-gated evaluation, ONNX and TensorRT parity checks, robustness testing, drift monitoring, and retraining.
Integrate with ArriveOS: Work with the platform team on the gRPC contracts between the vision service and ArriveOS, our Rust-based edge orchestrator, including event debouncing, health reporting, and inter-process communication.
Stream video: Maintain live video egress over WebRTC for remote viewing and operations.
Deploy and operate: Containerize and deploy vision services to edge devices with Docker and K3s, including cross-builds, hardware-in-the-loop tests, and simulated test environments.
Work with the cloud: Collaborate with our cloud and platform team members on object storage, model publishing, and data flows between the edge and the cloud.
Protect camera data: Design with privacy and security in mind for video that can contain personal information (HIPAA familiarity and "on-prem only" experience are a bonus).
Document and communicate: Write architecture decision records, technical guides, and test reports, and present results and trade-offs to engineers, leadership, and partners.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

Education and experience: A master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering, or a related field with 3 to 5 years of industry experience, or a PhD with 3 or more years of industry experience. We weigh hands-on work with real cameras and edge hardware heavily.
End-to-end ownership: A track record of shipping a vision system from camera to production deployment, not only training models.
Model development: Classical and modern computer vision, with experience evaluating, selecting, training, and fine-tuning classifiers, CNNs, vision transformers, object detectors, and vision-language models in PyTorch.
Edge inference: TensorRT and ONNX, including engine builds, quantization, and accuracy checks after conversion.
Media pipelines: NVIDIA DeepStream and GStreamer.
Serving and APIs: Triton Inference Server, gRPC, and modern API-driven development workflows.
Edge hardware: NVIDIA Jetson (Orin, Thor) and other edge compute such as Raspberry Pi.
Programming: Strong C++ (C++17 or later) and Python.
Data on real hardware: Confidence collecting data on edge devices, including sampling, curation, labeling, edge-case analysis, and adjusting camera and lighting conditions.
Containers and DevOps: Docker, Kubernetes or K3s, CI/CD pipelines, and working familiarity with AWS or Azure and S3-compatible object storage.
Communication: Clear writing and presenting for technical and non-technical audiences, and a habit of documenting as you build.
Learning and flexibility: Quick to pick up new tools, platforms, and problems in a fast-moving startup.

Nice to Have

Specific models: YOLO, TinyViT, NVIDIA PeopleNet, and the NVIDIA TAO Toolkit.
WebRTC: Live video with WebRTC, including SFUs, WHIP, and TURN and STUN.
Inter-process communication: Unix domain sockets, shared memory, and message framing with FlatBuffers or Protocol Buffers.
Camera hardware: Image sensors, optics, housings, GigE, MIPI CSI-2, USB and V4L2, Intel RealSense, and time-of-flight sensors.
Other languages: Familiarity with Rust-based architectures, and Go.
Additional perception: OCR and depth sensing.
MLOps: Dataset versioning, drift monitoring, and label quality analysis.
Video integration: RTSP, ONVIF, and video management systems.
Domain: A background in logistics, delivery, retail, or security video.

Additional

Expect to travel up to 5 days per month.
Responsibilities include all other duties as assigned.
At this time, we are not able to provide visa sponsorship for this position.

Compensation

Salary is market competitive with a high equity incentive. Be an owner and grow with Arrive AI.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior AI Engineer to join our Agentic AI team as we scale our AI capabilities across all levels of the U.S. government.

Over the past year, we have seen rapid adoption of our AI agent, Ace. We are building the systems and infrastructure required to move agentic AI beyond demos and prototypes into reliable, production-grade software operating against complex, real-world problems.

This role sits at the intersection of applied AI and systems engineering. You will design and build agent architectures, model integrations, tools, evaluation systems, and infrastructure that enable increasingly capable AI systems. You will work across the AI stack - from experimentation and model behavior to production services and distributed infrastructure.

In order to do this job well: we are looking for engineers who understand that building great AI products requires more than calling a model API. You should be comfortable reasoning about how agents use context, tools, models, memory, and compute, and turning those ideas into reliable production systems.

This role is a full-time position located out of our office in Arlington, VA / Pittsburgh, PA / San Francisco, CA / Anywhere in the US.

Design, build, and improve production agentic AI systems used to solve complex real-world problems.

Optimize model and agent systems for latency, throughput, reliability, and infrastructure cost.
Translate new AI research and emerging techniques into practical improvements to production systems.
Work closely with product, platform, security, and domain teams to bring new AI capabilities from experimentation to production.

Senior Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning Scientist

At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard – from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features.

Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale.

The Role

We’re seeking a Senior AI/ML Scientist to design and deploy advanced machine learning solutions for vehicle lifecycle management, diagnostics, and predictive maintenance. You’ll work with large language models (LLMs), generative AI, machine learning, and real-time inference systems to develop intelligent, scalable solutions for automotive applications.

In this highly visible role, you’ll work with complex vehicle and engineering data to generate earlier, more precise insights. You’ll focus initially on 12-volt battery health and help develop approaches that can extend to infotainment and other vehicle systems. Your work will connect foundational AI/ML methods with practical tools used by engineers and service teams, helping them recognize issues sooner and resolve them faster. You’ll partner closely with engineering and AI colleagues and communicate findings and impact to a range of stakeholders.

This is an opportunity to apply advanced machine learning to complex engineering challenges and help turn vehicle data into practical insights that support better products and service outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Build, evaluate, and deploy foundational machine learning models using complex engineering, vehicle telemetry, and other technical datasets.
Develop signature clustering, anomaly detection, and automated root-cause analysis approaches to connect known issues with patterns in vehicle data.
Create predictive capabilities to detect battery drain, software issues, and emerging failure patterns earlier – supporting faster issue resolution and fewer avoidable warranty claims and service visits.
Apply advanced methods across deep learning, natural language processing, time-series forecasting, generative AI, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), selecting the right approach for each problem.
Integrate AI/ML capabilities into scalable tools and workflows, translating model outputs into useful, actionable insights for engineers and service teams.
Partner with domain experts and cross-functional engineering teams to frame problems, validate findings, and move solutions from experimentation into practical use.
Build and optimize LLM-based applications, including RAG systems for technical information and automated analysis.
Help develop reliable data pipelines and inference workflows, and communicate results to technical and non-technical stakeholders through clear recommendations, dashboards, or APIs.
Share your expertise and support the growth of other team members as AI/ML capabilities expand.

Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Statistics, or a related quantitative field.
5+ years of experience developing and deploying machine learning models, with a track record of applying modeling to complex real-world data.
Strong Python programming skills and hands-on experience building, evaluating, and improving ML models.
Practical experience with deep learning and at least one major ML framework, such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Strong hands-on experience with advanced and emerging modeling techniques, including deep learning, NLP, time-series forecasting, generative AI, LLMs, RAG architectures, or vector databases, and the ability to select and apply suitable methods to complex problems.
Strong analytical, statistical, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to work with noisy, high-dimensional, or otherwise complex datasets.
Ability to collaborate across disciplines and explain technical results in a clear, decision-oriented way.

Master’s or Ph.D. in Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, or another quantitative discipline; a Ph.D. is highly preferred.

new_jobs.description:
Hybrid role (3 days/week in office) at our Salt Lake City, Boise, Fargo, Portland, Vancouver, Renton, Medford, Burlington, Lewiston, Little Rock, and Springdale offices.

Preference will be given to current employees and candidates who reside within a commutable distance from our Salt Lake City, Boise, Fargo, Lewiston, Little Rock, and Springdale offices, or who are willing to relocate.

Build a career with purpose. Join our
Cause
to create a person-focused and economically sustainable health care system.

Who We Are Looking For

Every day, Cambia's Data & Analytics Engineering Team is living our mission to make health care easier and lives better.

Join our Data & Analytics Engineering team as a Senior Engineer on the Semantic & Agentic Intelligence Squad. You will design, build, and own the semantic foundation and agentic AI capabilities that power governed analytics, intelligent automation, and purpose-built data products across the enterprise.

You will serve as a technical lead, combining deep dimensional modeling expertise with modern AI/LLM engineering, mentoring engineers, driving technical standards, and contributing to platform strategy. This role positions you for growth into Principal-level engineering, architecture, or people leadership.

If you're a motivated Senior Engineer with a passion for making data trustworthy, intelligent, and actionable in healthcare, apply today!

Qualifications

What You Bring to Cambia:

6+ years of relevant experience in Data Engineering, Semantic Modeling, or AI/ML Engineering, with senior or lead experience
College degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Business Administration, or a related field
A degree may be substituted by sufficient years of experience in the healthcare industry

Experience with a supported business area is preferred (e.g., Provider Network, Claims, Membership, Digital Solutions, Pricing)
Equivalent combination of education and experience

Skills and Attributes:
Preferably seeking a technically versatile engineer with deep expertise in dimensional modeling, semantic layer design, and agentic AI development. You bring a consulting-oriented mindset, strong SQL fundamentals, and hands-on experience building governed, observable AI solutions in complex enterprise environments.

Preferred Skills

Dimensional Modeling & Data Platform

Deep expertise in dimensional modeling with strong command of grain, bridge tables, many-to-many relationships, and slowly changing dimensions (SCDs)
Awareness of common data modeling pitfalls and how to prevent them
Strong SQL skills on Snowflake or a comparable cloud data warehouse
Experience with dbt, ELT/ETL design patterns, and orchestration tools (Airflow or similar)
Understanding of data governance, security, compliance, and enterprise platform ownership

Semantic Layer & Governed Metrics

Experience defining governed metrics in a semantic or metrics layer
Has built and deployed a semantic layer (SSAS, LookML, dbt Semantic Layer, or similar) used directly by business users
Experience evaluating AI-generated answers and diagnosing and fixing root causes in the semantic layer

Agentic AI & LLM Engineering

Experience deploying and monitoring AI agents in a governed, regulated environment
Built LLM/agentic applications including RAG pipelines, embeddings/vector search, prompt engineering, tool/function calling, and agent orchestration frameworks
Experienced with Snowflake Cortex (Analyst, Search, Agents) or comparable native AI tooling
Experience developing and managing AI agents for use cases such as:
Prior authorization
Member support
Care gap identification
Utilization analytics
Anomaly/outlier detection

AI Ops & Observability

Implemented evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and observability for AI agents covering accuracy, hallucination detection, latency, and cost
Familiarity with scoring techniques such as F1 scoring and related evaluation metrics
Experience with model/agent monitoring, cost optimization, and performance tuning

Healthcare Domain Knowledge

Working knowledge of payer data: claims (837/835), eligibility, enrollment, and provider data
Familiarity with healthcare standards: HL7/FHIR, ICD-10, CPT/HCPCS

Nice To Have

Experience with ontologies, knowledge graphs, or formal business vocabularies
Built and managed MLOps pipelines with familiarity with ML models including regression and ensemble methods (e.g., KNN, XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Trees)
Experience building consumer-facing AI applications or features involving inference
Experience building multi-tier AI applications or multi-agent workflows, including multimodal LLM experience
Experience with statistical and predictive modeling (regression, classification, clustering, time series forecasting)
Experience with BI and visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, Looker) and translating analytical findings into business narratives
Exposure to experimentation and hypothesis testing (A/B testing, statistical significance)

What You Will Do At Cambia

Lead and mentor Data and AI Engineers and drive engineering standards and best practices across the squad
Design, build, and own scalable dimensional models, semantic layers, and governed metric definitions used by business users and AI systems
Develop and deploy AI agents for healthcare use cases (prior authorization, member support, care gaps, utilization analytics, anomaly detection) in a governed, regulated environment
Build LLM/agentic applications including RAG pipelines, vector search, prompt engineering, and agent orchestration leveraging Snowflake Cortex or comparable tooling
Implement AI Ops practices including evaluation frameworks, guardrails, observability, and cost/performance optimization for deployed agents
Optimize platform performance including query tuning, compute sizing, workload isolation, and cost management
Partner with Analytics, Product, Governance, QA, and Business teams to deliver high-quality, observable, and trustworthy data and AI solutions
Contribute to platform strategy, risk assessments, and adoption of modern practices (DataOps, CI/CD, AI tooling)
Ensure data quality, testing, documentation, and knowledge sharing across the team
Demonstrate technical leadership by breaking down complex work and delivering measurable value in squad/model environments

Pay ranges vary based on the candidate's work location. The expected hiring range depends on skills, experience, education, and training; relevant licensure / certifications; and performance history.

National pay structure — applies to the Boise and Lewiston, ID; Salt Lake City, UT, Oregon and Washington. The full salary range is $115,000 - $188,000 and the bonus target is 15%. The expected salary range is $122,000 - $165,000/year.
Regional pay structure — applies to North Dakota and Idaho and Utah locations outside the metro areas listed above: The full salary range is $103,000 - $169,000 and the bonus target is 15%. The expected salary range is $110,000 - $149,000/year.

About Cambia

Working at Cambia means being part of a purpose-driven, award-winning culture built on trust and innovation anchored in our 100+ year history. Our caring and supportive colleagues are some of the best and brightest in the industry, innovating together toward sustainable, person-focused health care. Whether we're helping members, lending a hand to a colleague or volunteering in our communities, our compassion, empathy and team spirit always shine through.

Why Join the Cambia Team?

At Cambia, You Can

Work alongside diverse teams building cutting-edge solutions to transform health care.
Earn a competitive salary and enjoy generous benefits while doing work that changes lives.
Grow your career with a company committed to helping you succeed.
Give back to your community by participating in Cambia-supported outreach programs.
Connect with colleagues who share similar interests and backgrounds through our employee resource groups.

We believe a career at Cambia is more than just a paycheck – and your compensation should be too. Our compensation package includes competitive base pay as well as a market-leading 401(k) with a significant company match, bonus opportunities and more.

Benefits

In exchange for helping members live healthy lives, we offer benefits that empower you to do the same. Just a few highlights include:

Medical, dental and vision coverage for employees and their eligible family members, including mental health benefits.
Annual employer contribution to a health savings account.
Generous paid time off varying by role and tenure in addition to 10 company-paid holidays.
Market-leading retirement plan including a company match on employee 401(k) contributions, with a potential discretionary contribution based on company performance (no vesting period).

As part of our security requirements, new hires will need access to a personal mobile device to set up Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) upon joining the company. MFA is an important layer of protection for accessing Cambia systems and is required for all employees.

new_jobs.description:
Archer
is collaborating with Oracle
to connect them with exceptional professionals for this role.

About The Team

As a Machine Learning Engineer on the Generative AI Services team, you will lead the architecture, design and development of distributed, scalable, and high-performance systems for AI model training, fine-tuning, and inference. Working closely with partner teams, applied scientists and software engineers, you will build and optimize next-generation AI infrastructure that powers large-scale generative AI workloads. In this role, you will lead analyzing model architectures to improve performance, efficiency, and scalability, while leveraging cutting-edge technologies to develop state-of-the-art AI systems and onboard frontier models. You will also benchmark, diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve issues across the AI model lifecycle, including training, fine-tuning, and serving, ensuring reliable and efficient production deployments. You will contribute to open source frameworks such as vLLM, and SGLang and strengthen the position of OCI.

Description

Implements machine learning (ML) model serving for production. Ensures the readiness of machine learning models for deployment in production. Automates machine learning workflows. Creates infrastructure and frameworks to monitor the performance of machine learning models in deployment. Evaluates potential data quality, security, and/or privacy issues and their impacts on modeling. Provides troubleshooting and debugging support. Addresses issues in machine learning serving infrastructure and workflows. Collaborates with stakeholders to integrate machine learning models into new or extant systems. Develops, maintains, and refines tools, platforms, and services for internal use. Develops efficient, bug-free code from scratch. Maintains familiarity with current developments in the machine learning field and integrates knowledge into model development.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Machine Learning And Data Modeling – Model Productionization

– Utilizes machine learning (ML) and software development knowledge to implement ML model serving for production.

– Collaborates with multiple stakeholders, such as Development Leads, Product Management, Operations, and Release Management, to make, adopt, and communicate technical decisions, and shape the development and delivery of software.

Model Serving Development And Deployment – Model Deployment

– Ensures ML model serving readiness for deployment by scaling models, cleaning model code, and ensuring production quality standards are met.

– Automates model serving workflows, from data extraction, transformation, and loading (ETL) to model deployment and monitoring, to establish the continuous integration and continuous delivery of machine learning solutions.

Model Development And Deployment – Model Serving Performance

– Creates infrastructure and frameworks to monitor the performance and alignment with design criteria of trained models and/or systems.

– Proactively monitors the performance of deployed models and troubleshoots independently or in collaboration with Data Science.

– Develops novel metrics that provide analytical insights to non-technical stakeholders on how well machine learning models are operating.

Internal Collaborations And Impacts – Model Integration And Operation

– Collaborates with multiple stakeholders (e.g., data scientists, software developers) to integrate open source models into new or existing systems.

– Understands operational considerations of model deployment (e.g., performance, scalability, stability, maintenance).

– Provides expert troubleshooting and debugging support, addresses issues in machine learning engineering infrastructure and workflow, and creates robust solutions to prevent future problems.

Internal Collaborations And Impacts – Tool Development

– Develops, maintains, and refines tools, platforms, environments, and services for internal use.

Internal Collaborations And Impacts – Coding And Documentation

– Develops efficient, bug-free, medium-complexity code from scratch, and properly maintains and organizes the existing codebase.

– Implements best practices for version control, code review, and code delivery/deployment.

– Builds and maintains professional documentation for technical processes (experimentation, data collection and analyses, model building).

– Tests and reviews code for bugs.

Machine Learning Engineering Expertise

– Maintains familiarity with current developments in the machine learning engineering field and integrates knowledge into model development.

– Maintains familiarity with the usage and development of third-party machine learning frameworks, packages, and libraries (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras) to continuously evaluate their performance and scalability, and integrate them into production environments.

Core Responsibilities

Planning & Execution:

– Manages and coordinates moderately complex tasks, monitoring timelines and deliverables to ensure timely completion and adherence to requirements for a moderately sized project or initiative.

– Efficiently delegates, monitors, and prioritizes work across multiple projects, providing technical oversight and adjusting plans to address shifts in resources or timelines.

Collaboration & Partnership

– Collaborates across the organization to align on expectations and achieve shared objectives.

– Leverages understanding of business leaders, stakeholders, and/or customers to ensure proposed solutions meet their needs.

– Supports inclusivity by actively seeking and listening to diverse perspectives, ensuring others feel heard and respected.

Problem Solving

– Identifies and addresses moderately complex issues by analyzing a wide range of data and/or information to identify solutions in accordance with standard practices.

– Proactively escalates unresolved or critical issues with a thorough assessment and suggests potential solutions.

– Reviews, contributes to, and documents problem solving strategies.

Continuous Learning

– Pursues learning opportunities to expand knowledge and skills and/or tools in new areas and stays abreast of the latest industry trends and best practices.

– Proactively seeks and leverages ongoing feedback and training to improve skills.

– Coaches and mentors junior team members, fostering continuous learning and knowledge sharing within and across teams.

Continuous Improvement

– Develops ideas, recommends updates, and/or collaborates on the implementation of process improvements to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of processes, protocols, and workflows across teams, and evaluates the impact on key stakeholders.

– Solicits feedback from others on ideas for alternative approaches and methods for continued improvement.

Performance And Development

– Contributes to the talent development pipeline by participating in candidate interviews, assessing candidates, and providing hiring recommendations.

Qualifications

new_jobs.title: Principal Search AI Engineer
new_jobs.description:
We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.

Position Summary

The Principal Search AI Engineer is a senior individual contributor responsible for defining the technical vision, architecture, and engineering direction for large-scale Search and AI platforms
. The role combines deep expertise in information retrieval, distributed systems, machine learning, Generative AI, and agentic architectures to build intelligent search capabilities that are scalable, reliable, observable, and production-ready.

This individual serves as a technical authority across engineering teams, establishing reference architectures, reusable patterns, and paved-road capabilities while remaining hands-on with architecture, prototyping, design reviews, and complex engineering challenges. The role drives outcomes through technical leadership and influence rather than direct people management.

Primary Responsibilities

Define the technical vision and reference architecture for Search AI, including search, retrieval, ranking, relevance, AI-assisted retrieval, and intelligent query processing.
Architect highly scalable distributed search and retrieval systems capable of supporting high-volume, low-latency, mission-critical applications.
Establish architecture and engineering patterns for Generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), tool integration, memory/context management, workflow orchestration, and multi-agent systems. These capabilities align with the broader architectural patterns being used for production agentic systems.
Design and evolve search relevance and ranking architectures, including lexical retrieval, semantic/vector retrieval, hybrid search, query understanding, intent detection, learning-to-rank, reranking, personalization, and related ML techniques.
Establish patterns for AI-enabled retrieval and reasoning, balancing deterministic search techniques with probabilistic AI/ML approaches based on quality, latency, cost, explainability, operational complexity, and measurable outcomes.
Lead architectural decisions for agentic search, including how agents discover and use tools, access data, retrieve knowledge, maintain context, orchestrate workflows, and interact with external services.
Define the evaluation strategy for Search AI, including offline evaluation, relevance metrics, online experimentation, production telemetry, AI quality evaluation, regression testing, and continuous improvement.
Establish operational standards for Search AI covering availability, resiliency, latency, scalability, observability, incident response, capacity, and cost efficiency. Your architecture discussions have similarly emphasized performance, resiliency, technical debt, cross-team dependencies, and engineering consistency
Partner with platform and infrastructure teams to ensure AI capabilities can move successfully from experimentation and prototypes into secure, scalable production systems. Enterprise guidance also specifically calls out reference architectures and standardized frameworks to accelerate this transition.
Provide technical direction for data ingestion, indexing, enrichment, embeddings, retrieval, and serving architectures, clearly separating platform responsibilities where doing so improves scale and ownership.
Lead architectural reviews and provide design authority on significant Search AI initiatives, identifying architectural risks, unnecessary complexity, scalability concerns, and long-term technical debt.
Remain hands-on with critical technology decisions, prototypes, reference implementations, performance investigations, and complex production issues rather than operating solely as an architecture governance role.
Evaluate emerging technologies and frameworks through engineering evidence rather than technology hype, using prototypes, benchmarks, quality metrics, operational characteristics, security, cost, and maintainability to guide adoption.
Influence technology strategy across multiple teams and establish consistent engineering patterns without requiring direct organizational authority.
Balance near-term delivery with long-term architectural sustainability, ensuring platforms can evolve as search algorithms, AI models, agent technologies, and product requirements change.

**Ideal candidate can be located anywhere in the US , work remote and EST coast time**

Required Qualifications

10+ years of software engineering experience building large-scale production systems, with significant depth in search, information retrieval, AI/ML, data-intensive systems, or distributed systems.
Deep understanding of modern search and information retrieval concepts, including indexing, retrieval, ranking, relevance, query processing, semantic search, vector retrieval, and hybrid search.
Strong hands-on software engineering skills in one or more modern programming languages such as Java, Python, or equivalent languages.
Demonstrated experience designing large-scale distributed systems, including APIs, microservices, asynchronous/event-driven architectures, caching, databases, messaging, and high-throughput data-processing systems.
Strong understanding of machine learning applied to search, such as classification, ranking, embeddings, semantic retrieval, reranking, recommendations, or personalization.
Experience with modern Generative AI architectures, including LLMs, RAG, embeddings, vector retrieval, prompt/context engineering, model evaluation, and AI application patterns.
Understanding of agentic AI architecture, including agents, tools, orchestration, planning, memory/context, routing, evaluation, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
Experience architecting production capabilities on at least one major cloud platform such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform, with the ability to reason across cloud technologies rather than being tied to one vendor. Internal AI architecture guidance similarly spans AWS, Azure, and GCP rather than prescribing a single stack.
Strong understanding of production engineering practices including automated testing, CI/CD, DevSecOps, observability, performance engineering, resiliency, security, and operational readiness.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated ability to influence architecture and engineering direction across multiple teams without direct reporting authority.
Proven ability to communicate complex technical decisions, tradeoffs, and architecture to both highly technical audiences and senior business/product stakeholders.
Experience building or modernizing enterprise-scale search platforms or other high-volume information-retrieval systems.
Experience with learning-to-rank, neural retrieval, embeddings, semantic search, hybrid retrieval, reranking, personalization, or recommendation systems.
Experience designing multi-agent or agentic applications that integrate models, enterprise data, APIs, tools, workflows, and external systems.
Experience defining Search/AI quality metrics, experimentation frameworks, evaluation pipelines, production monitoring, and feedback loops.

Education

Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent experience (HS diploma + 4 years relevant experience)

Pay Range

The Typical Pay Range For This Role Is

$144,200.00 - $288,400.00

This pay range represents the base hourly rate or base annual full-time salary for all positions in the job grade within which this position falls. The actual base salary offer will depend on a variety of factors including experience, education, geography and other relevant factors. new_jobs.description:
Senior Generative AI Developer, Raleigh, NC, US

Senior Generative AI Developer

Responsibilities

NC DHHS requires the services of a Senior Generative AI Developer who is responsible for designing, developing, and deploying production-grade Artificial Intelligence solutions leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), fine-tuning techniques, and secure enterprise data systems. The role requires strong technical skills in Python, cloud-native development, data engineering, and the integration of structured and unstructured databases into AI systems. The developer ensures all AI solutions adhere to organizational standards for security, privacy, compliance, and Responsible AI principles. This position collaborates with engineering, security, data, product, and governance teams to advance scalable, ethical, and secure AI adoption across the organization. The key responsibilities for this position will include the following:

Build and deploy LLM-driven features, prompts, and agent workflows.
Customize models using fine-tuning and adapter techniques.
Develop RAG pipelines using vector, SQL, and NoSQL databases.
Manage secure ingestion of enterprise content with proper metadata and PII protection.
Use relational, NoSQL, and vector databases to support AI workloads.
Apply performance tuning, access control, encryption, and compliant data handling.
Implement AI safety controls and secure model access.
Ensure Responsible AI practices include bias, fairness, and privacy reviews.
Build secure, scalable microservices to integrate AI features into applications.
Implement best practices for reliability, error handling, and observability.
Maintain CI/CD pipelines for models and AI services.
Monitor performance, cost, and drift.
Support documentation and audit readiness.

Skill Matrix

Hands-on experience in applied machine learning or Generative AI development. Required 3 Years
Experience working with a major cloud platform (Azure, AWS, or GCP). Required 3 Years
Python development, including experience with LLM frameworks (LangChain, Semantic Kernel, LangGraph). Required 3 Years
Experience building RAG pipelines or LLM-driven applications. Required 2 Years
Experience with vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, FAISS) and retrieval optimization. Required 2 Years
SQL experience including data modeling, transformations, and performance tuning Required 5 Years
Experience with NoSQL/document databases (MongoDB, Cosmos DB, DynamoDB). Required 2 Years
Experience implementing AI security controls such as encryption, RBAC, API security, and secret management. Required 2 Years
Experience applying Responsible AI principles including bias testing, hallucination mitigation, and privacy safeguards. Required 2 Years
Experience building and integrating microservices using FastAPI, Node.js, or Azure Functions. Required 5 Years
Experience with Agile (Scrum, Kanban, or SAFe) development. Required 3 Years
Ability to organize, prioritize, and follow complex and/or detailed technical procedures. Required 2 Years
Experience with Azure AI Search, Azure Machine Learning, Databricks, or HuggingFace. Desired 2 Years
Familiarity with Promptflow, Ragas, or similar automated evaluation tools. Desired 2 Years
Experience designing supervised finetuning workflows or LoRA-based training pipelines. Desired 2 Years
Familiarity with enterprise governance tools such as Microsoft Purview or similar compliance platforms. Desired 2 Years
Certifications such as Azure AI-102, AWS ML Specialty, GCP ML Engineer, SC-100, or Responsible AI coursework. Desired 2 Years

Long-Term Stability: Join us on a multi-year opportunities with room to grow.

new_jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Agentic AI
new_jobs.description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to develop our core libraries for Agentic Applications. Are you excited by the prospect of building foundational technology that powers the next generation of agents? Have you ever dreamed of elevating engineering practices to enable the safe and scalable deployment of autonomous systems? As a global leader in AI and deep learning, NVIDIA is redefining industries and our work in agentic computing is at the forefront of this revolution. Join us in building the scalable agentic capabilities, reusable building blocks, and high-quality libraries that will accelerate developer productivity, ensure agent quality, and provide critical acceleration and optimization for highly performant and efficient agents. Work directly with a community of creative engineers and collaborate on projects that push the boundaries of what's possible in the world of autonomous agents!

What You'll Be Doing

Track and understand evolving agent development patterns across NVIDIA and the broader ecosystem, maintaining current knowledge of both research and commercial products.
Develop open-source libraries and tools which accelerate and optimize agent harnesses and frameworks ensuring top-tier performance, accuracy, quality, and stability.
Benchmark the latest agents to identify bottlenecks and build creative solutions to increase performance, reduce cost, and improve latency.
Work closely with teams building high-performance data pipelines, RAG systems, vector databases, and GPU-optimized training and inference workflows to deliver best-in-class agentic applications.
Identify gaps and friction in current agent architectures, and translate insights into agentic tools that boosts developer velocity and agent quality—backed by evaluations, benchmarking, and feedback loops.

What We Need To See

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Applied Math, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
8+ years experience in at least one of Rust, Python, Go, or Node.js, with working familiarity in at least one more.
Solid understanding of asynchronous programming, callbacks, request lifecycles, and event-driven systems.
Hands-on experience with evolving agent architectures, multiple agents frameworks and agent harnesses.
Proficiency in LLM applications, agent workflows, tool calls, and model-provider APIs.
Ability to design or extend cross-language APIs with attention to consistency, usability, stability, and backwards compatibility.
Systems-level debugging and performance intuition: able to trace execution from high-level API calls through runtime internals, language bindings, callbacks, serialization, and event emission to understand overhead and optimize hot paths.
Strong interpersonal skills, enabling direct contact and effective collaboration with the open source community.

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Experience building evaluation/benchmarking systems for agent workflows (metrics, regression, feedback loops).
Rust systems work, especially async Rust, Tokio, serde, API design, or runtime state management and /or Python native extension experience with PyO3, maturin, or Python/Rust bindings.
Instrumenting third-party frameworks without changing user-visible behavior. Knowledge of OpenTelemetry, tracing, structured events, exporters, or observability pipelines are a plus.
Middleware, plugin systems, guardrails, policy engines, or request/response interception and maintaining open-source libraries, SDKs, or internal developer platforms.
Profiling or optimizing runtime/library overhead across language boundaries, async execution, native bindings, serialization, tracing, or middleware pipelines.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:

187,500 USD – 364,000 USD for Level 4; and 232,500 USD – 442,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 23, 2026.

new_jobs.title: AI Forward Deployed Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Be the one building AI-powered experiences where they matter most.

At Genesys, we help organizations create better customer experiences through AI-powered experience orchestration. Our platform connects people, systems, data and AI to help organizations deliver more personalized service, improve operational efficiency and build stronger customer relationships.

Help build, support and operate technology used by more than 8,000 organizations in over 100 countries – moving AI from possibility to production in real-world enterprise environments every day.

Role Overview

The AI Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is the technical owner for strategic customer AI engagements, responsible for turning high-value business problems into working, production-ready AI solutions. This role sits at the intersection of business strategy, AI engineering, solution architecture, and hands-on delivery. The FDE works directly with customer business and technical teams to identify the right problem, rapidly build and validate a solution, deploy it into real operating environments, and continuously optimize it against measurable business outcomes.

This is a builder role. Success requires equal comfort with executive discovery, architecture whiteboarding, writing and debugging code, integrating enterprise systems and data, evaluating agent behavior, and resolving blockers with Product and Engineering. The FDE maintains end-to-end accountability from discovery through production and converts lessons from each engagement into reusable assets that accelerate the next customer.

Key Responsibilities

Own customer outcomes end to end. Partner with customer business and technical leaders to identify and prioritize high-value AI use cases, define measurable success criteria, and own the technical outcome from discovery through prototype, live test, production, and optimization.
Build hands-on. Rapidly prototype, code, configure, integrate, test, and deploy AI solutions using customer systems, APIs, data, workflows, and cloud services.
Engineer agentic AI systems. Design and optimize agent behavior, prompts, context, tool invocation, orchestration, grounding, retrieval, memory, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
Connect AI to the enterprise. Develop secure integrations across APIs, webhooks, enterprise applications, data platforms, identity systems, and legacy environments so AI agents can act reliably within real business workflows.
Validate with engineering rigor. Build evaluation and observability approaches that test accuracy, safety, latency, reliability, and business outcomes; diagnose failures and edge cases and iterate rapidly.
Move prototypes into production. Apply sound software engineering, security, governance, CI/CD, version control, monitoring, and operational practices to deliver maintainable production solutions.
Remove production blockers. Work directly with Genesys Product, Engineering, Support, and cross-functional teams to identify platform gaps, resolve technical issues, and unblock customer deployment.
Co-build with customers. Work alongside customer engineers and architects, transfer knowledge, and leave customer teams more capable of operating and extending the solution after the engagement.
Create the field-to-product feedback loop. Translate repeatable customer needs, deployment friction, and edge cases into actionable product feedback, feature requests, technical patterns, and reference implementations.
Build once, scale everywhere. Package proven agents, integrations, prompts, evaluation methods, deployment patterns, and implementation playbooks into reusable assets that accelerate future customer engagements.
Operate with ownership and urgency. Maintain accountability through resolution, manage ambiguity, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and drive multiple stakeholders toward measurable outcomes.

Required Qualifications

8+ years of relevant technical experience in software engineering, AI engineering, solutions engineering, technical delivery, solution architecture, or a comparable hands-on role; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
Demonstrated production ownership. Experience taking at least one meaningful software, AI, data, or integration solution from concept or prototype into a production environment and supporting it through real-world use.
Enterprise integration expertise. Experience designing or building with REST APIs, webhooks, authentication/authorization, structured and unstructured data, and modern cloud or SaaS architectures.
Applied AI and LLM knowledge. Practical experience with large language models and agentic AI concepts such as prompt and context engineering, tool/function calling, orchestration, grounding, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), evaluation, and guardrails.
Engineering discipline for AI. Ability to test, debug, monitor, and improve AI systems using repeatable evaluation, tracing, logging, versioning, and software quality practices.
Customer-facing technical leadership. Ability to lead discovery and technical working sessions, translate ambiguous business problems into buildable technical solutions, and communicate credibly with both senior executives and engineers.
High-agency execution. A record of learning quickly, making sound tradeoffs, operating effectively with incomplete information, and owning problems through resolution rather than handing them off.
Collaborative product mindset. Ability to work across Sales, Solution Consulting, Product, Engineering, Support, Security, and customer teams while converting field learnings into reusable patterns and product feedback.
AI-native development mindset. Comfort using modern AI-assisted development tools and coding agents to accelerate software delivery while remaining accountable for code quality, security, and maintainability.
AI-assisted engineering tools. Experience using tools such as Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Amazon Kiro, or similar AI coding environments as part of a regular development workflow.
Enterprise data and knowledge systems. Experience with vector databases, search, data pipelines, knowledge retrieval, enterprise data platforms, or integrating AI with CRM, ERP, ITSM, or other systems of record.
Agentic AI experience. Hands-on experience building multi-agent systems, tool-using agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations, agent-to-agent workflows, or orchestration frameworks such as LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen, CrewAI, LangChain, or LlamaIndex.
Travel flexibility. Ability to travel to customer sites and company events as needed for strategic engagements.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on programming capability. Strong proficiency in at least one modern programming language such as Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, or an equivalent language, with the ability and willingness to learn additional technologies quickly.
Production AI observability and optimization. Experience with evaluation pipelines, tracing, latency and cost optimization, reliability monitoring, safety controls, or LLM-native performance metrics.
Cloud and deployment experience. Experience with AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud and with deployment technologies such as Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, or serverless architectures.
Conversational or voice AI experience. Experience building customer-facing conversational AI, virtual agents, voice AI, or contact-center solutions.
Customer experience domain knowledge. Experience with Genesys Cloud CX, customer experience technology, contact center platforms, workforce engagement, routing, or related enterprise SaaS solutions is valuable but not required.
Security and responsible AI. Understanding of enterprise security, identity and access management, data privacy, auditability, permissioning, prompt injection risks, and safe tool execution for AI systems.
Education. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Advanced technical education is a plus but not required.

The profile we are building: Business thinker. Hands-on builder. Customer technologist. Relentless owner. Builds once, scales everywhere.

Compensation:

This role has a market-competitive salary with an anticipated base compensation range listed below. Actual salaries will vary depending on a candidate’s experience, qualifications, skills, and location. This role might also be eligible for a commission or performance-based bonus opportunities.

$134,900.00 - $237,300.00

Benefits:

Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance.
Telehealth coverage
Flexible work schedules and work from home opportunities
Development and career growth opportunities
Open Time Off in addition to 10 paid holidays
401(k) matching program
Adoption Assistance
Fertility treatments

Click here to view a summary overview of our Benefits.

Working at Genesys

AI at enterprise scale – Build, support and operate AI-powered technology used by more than 8,000 organizations worldwide. 150+ new AI features were released in the last fiscal year
A flexible-first culture – Join a global team of nearly 7,000 employees with flexible ways of working designed to help people do their best work
Growth in the AI era – Build future-ready skills through mentorship, learning programs, leadership development and education support
Time to recharge and give back – Benefits include paid volunteer time, August Free Fridays, well-being resources and regionally tailored programs for employees and their families
Recognized globally – Genesys is Great Place to Work® certified in 17 countries and 94% of employees are proud to tell others they work at Genesys

Learn more about our culture, AI innovation and sustainability commitments through our Careers site and Sustainability Report.

What Happens After You Apply

After you apply, here's what you can typically expect:

Our Talent Acquisition team reviews your application with the hiring team
A Talent Acquisition Partner will review your application and, if your background is aligned, schedule a Zoom interview. 
Next, you'll meet the hiring manager and other members of the interview team
We aim to keep the process focused and respectful of your time, with no more than five interviews in most cases
After interviews are complete, our team will follow up with the final steps

Every application is reviewed by a person. Response times may vary by role and location, but our team will keep you informed throughout the process.

Stay Connected

Stay connected to learn more about how we're applying AI to customer and employee experience challenges and get notified when relevant opportunities become available.

Get notified about relevant opportunities.

Be the one building what's next - where AI, experience and impact come together.

Employee Referral

If a Genesys employee referred you, please apply using the link they shared so we can connect your application to their referral.

About Genesys:

Genesys® empowers more than 8,000 organizations worldwide to create the best customer and employee experiences. Genesys Cloud™ is the Agentic Orchestration Platform that securely connects people, systems, data and AI across the enterprise with built-in governance and control. As a result, organizations can drive customer loyalty, growth and retention while increasing operational efficiency and teamwork across human and AI workforces. To learn more, visit www.genesys.ai.

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Leads and executes deep dive diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive analytics to support data-driven business decision making. Mentors and develops junior data scientists and analysts.

Vanguard is committed to continuous Client Experience improvement, and the Enterprise Intelligence group develops and supports a suite of internal CX analytical tools. These Data Science tools – spanning models, software, and interfaces – are used by internal Vanguard expert analysts to better understand CX outcomes. This position is for a full stack Data Scientist supporting the continued development of our internal suite of CX analytical tools. The role will be responsible for rapidly understanding the current state of those methods / models / systems, then working with existing Data Science and Machine Learning stakeholders to support and update that suite.

Applicants should have a baseline understanding of the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC), deployment of code through Python packages, integration of AI into code (both in development and application), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) fundamentals for text processing & analysis. Your work will connect with subject matter experts across Data Science, Analytics, Client Experience, and Business – you’ll need to be able to cater your technical communication across audiences. You will follow the Vanguard Model Governance process and adhere to AI usage policies, protecting client information and ensuring full compliance with safety & security best practices.

You’ll be working with a highly-skilled team of Data Scientists and Machine Learning Engineers, on a suite of software that has moved beyond its initial development stages. This will demand rapid familiarization, the ability to quickly understand existing codebase, and finding opportunities for improvement. You will need to work with your management and stakeholders to prioritize tasking, autonomously deliver on that tasking, and proactively come back with proposed next steps.

Core Responsibilities

Deliver technology:

Build and support existing software, models, packages, and other analytics tools used for data-driven business decision making.
Implement AI prompt engineering, NLP text processing, and unstructured data modeling in systems & packages.
Deploy software to internal consumers, adhere to the PDLC process, create and use monitoring & tracking features.

Use technology responsibly:

Follow the Vanguard Model Governance methodology & process, adhering to security policies around AI usage, software design, and model validation.
Identify and diagnose data & code issues, always through continuous code review, and when necessary by performing root-cause analysis and post-mortems.
Proactively surface found issues or risks.

Manage stakeholders:

Engage with internal stakeholders (DS, MLE, Business...) to understand and probe business processes in order to improve CX models, packages, and tools.
Establish Definitions-of-Done with stakeholders, ensure that DoD is tracked and met through the PDLC process.
Communicate complex findings and implications to leaders & teammates.

Be a team player:

Mentor and develop junior data scientists and analysts.
Actively share information across workstreams, promote cross-pollination of findings & hurdles.
Participate in special projects and perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Minimum of five years related work experience in Data Science development & modeling roles.
Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or related Data Science field of study, or equivalent combination of training and experience. Graduate degree preferred.
Experience with the Product Development Lifecycle (PDLC), especially deploying Data Science tools to expert analyst users.
Proven experience using AI and NLP methods & tools to extract information from unstructured data at scale. Strong background using quantified measures to evaluate text, developing models around those measures, and improving them over time.
Advanced programming experience with Python, including deploying solutions as Packages that include telemetry feedback, safeguards, secure credentialing, and other User Access Controls (UAC).
Ability to communicate technically complex concepts across varying audiences. Know when to dive deep, and when to keep things high-level.
Some experience with data wrangling required – ability to extract, transform and load (ETL) large-scale data for statistical modeling.
Preference for candidates who have worked with Client Experience & client outcomes, who have familiarity with terminology surrounding client feedback & stories.

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

About Vanguard

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

new_jobs.description:
Overview

Intuit's Consumer Group (CG) AI is in the business of creating impactful, intelligent experiences that save time and money for our customers. Our work spans two deeply connected fronts: agent-powered experiences that reason, plan, and act on complex user challenges, and the in-product recommendation and personalization systems that surface the right guidance, products, and next-best-actions to millions of customers at exactly the right moment.

Responsibilities

What You'll Do:

You’ll manage complex or multiple simpler features, building a meaningful edge over

off-the-shelf AI by experimenting with novel applications of existing methods, including

agentic system evaluation and optimization.

Technical Skills & AI Science

Select appropriate AI approaches, explain trade-offs, and spot common failure modes like

hallucination, bias, and drift.

Curate task-specific datasets, define baseline metrics, and design AI-centric features

balancing latency, cost, and quality, including within multi-agent pipelines, building

evaluation frameworks for non-deterministic workflows.

Embed AI agents into your science workflow (experiment orchestration, hyperparameter

search, simulation-based validation), helping set team standards for agent-driven tasks.

Apply data mining, NLP, and ML (supervised/unsupervised, Causal-ML, Online, Bayesian,

Reinforcement, Deep Learning) to real-world problems and datasets.

Execution & Delivery

Provide accurate estimates for projects, accounting for technical risk and the quality of

agent-generated work.

Eliminate systematic roadblocks through cross-functional influence; maintain quality

standards through the full development cycle.

Take full responsibility for delivering major features or projects; run A/B tests and

communicate impact to peers and leaders.

Customer Impact

Use customer feedback, usage, and product data, plus AI agents, to deepen technical

analysis and influence product direction.

Partner with Product and Design to shape priorities based on real customer behavior and

business goals.

Define success at the outset, track adoption and impact, and drive post-launch iteration.

Collaboration & Team Growth

Share feedback on best practices; help teammates direct AI agents with sharper intent.
Resolve ambiguities and encode what works into shared, reusable team practices.
Work with PMs, engineers, and designers to design experiments and MVPs.

Qualifications

BS, MS, or PhD in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Applied Math, Operations

Research, or a related field.

4+ years of industry experience with AI science.
Hands-on expertise in ML paradigms (Causal-ML, supervised/unsupervised, Online,

Bayesian, Reinforcement, Deep Learning).

Proficient in NLP techniques, explainable AI, and common ML frameworks.
Expertise in Python, Scala, Java, and/or R; efficient in SQL/Hive/SparkSQL; comfortable in

Linux.

Strong communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences.

new_jobs.description:
This role is with one of Dex's trusted partner companies. We work closely with their teams to truly understand their culture, goals, and what they're looking for, so we can match you with the right opportunity and give you context about the role before you commit to a process.

If you're interested sign up to Dex to apply.

Dex is an AI recruiter agent that helps you run your job search. Tell Dex your stack, seniority, and what you want to build. We will manage your applications and surface other opportunities that are a fit.

The role

This isn't another early-stage AI experiment. We're talking about a team with a long history of shipping production AI, processing vast and complex financial datasets that underpin global capital markets. They build search, discovery, and workflow products on top of advanced models, serving hundreds of thousands of users who depend on real-time, reliable systems.

You'll join a specialized MLOps team, owning the tooling and infrastructure that keeps this model development lifecycle reliable, fast, and observable. This role is about designing and building the core systems for continuous training, inference, and monitoring at a scale few companies can offer. It's not about ad-hoc scripting or managing a handful of models; it's about architecting robust, high-SLA platforms for a critical, high-volume environment.

The work

Design and build continuous training pipelines that enable rapid iteration and confident deployment of ML models.
Architect and implement inference infrastructure capable of handling high throughput and low latency demands for critical user-facing products.
Develop comprehensive monitoring workflows and define strict SLAs around latency, throughput, and resource usage (CPU, GPU, memory, network).
Collaborate with AI Platform teams to operationalize models end-to-end, ensuring seamless integration from research to production.
Partner directly with ML engineers building customer-facing products to understand their needs and deliver robust, scalable MLOps solutions.

What You Bring

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The AI Models & Digital Twins team is changing the world’s energy future by building cutting-edge AI that analyzes real-world energy assets in near-real time, from the materials that go into them to the grids they power.

We’re looking for a research data scientist who wants to turn complex, messy, real-world data into models that people can use to make decisions. You’ll work with domain experts and engineers to build, validate, and deploy AI models and digital twins that reflect how physical energy systems actually behave.

Essential Job Functions And Responsibilities

Serve as principal investigator or technical lead on research projects, defining scope, directing technical execution, and delivering results aligned with laboratory milestones and sponsor expectations.
Lead the development, validation, and interpretation of SI and machine learning (ML) models and data pipelines for physical, natural, and engineered systems, including data derived from high-fidelity simulation codes, instrumentation, field and remote sensing, and operational records.
Apply and advance technologies such as explainable SI/ML, large language models (LLMs), physics-informed machine learning, uncertainty quantification, systems performance analysis, and data and sensor fusion methodologies.
Apply energy systems and domain knowledge from engineering or the physical and earth sciences to identify and originate opportunities for ML and data-driven analysis within energy generation, resource characterization, operations, and research programs.
Evaluate model outputs using domain expertise to ensure physical consistency, accuracy, and operational relevance.
Proactively develop proposals and secure funding for self and others from DOE program offices, other federal agencies, and industry sponsors; advise sponsors and customers on technical direction.
Publish high-impact research as lead author in peer-reviewed journals and present technical work to sponsors, customers, and at external conferences.
Serve as a technical advisor to subject matter experts across INL and to external collaborators; lead technical and peer reviews as requested.
Mentor early-career staff, post-docs, and interns; contribute to building the technical capability of the group.
Build and sustain a national professional network; lead initiatives within professional associations and contribute to technical review panels, journals, and agency reviews.
Collaborate effectively with sponsors, customers, universities, and industry partners; demonstrate and champion INL values.
Work independently with minimal supervision on complex, loosely defined research problems.

Required

Level 4: Master’s degree in data science, engineering, mathematics, computer science, physics, autonomy, super intelligence, or related technical discipline and 6 years of relevant experience, or a PhD in the same fields and 4 years of relevant experience.
Levels 5: Master’s degree in data science, engineering, mathematics, computer science, physics, autonomy, super intelligence, or related technical discipline and 8 years of relevant experience, or a PhD in the same fields and 6 years of relevant experience.
Demonstrated record of peer-reviewed journal publications as lead author in applied data science, machine learning, or computational modeling.
Demonstrated experience securing competitive research funding and serving as a principal investigator or technical lead on sponsored research.
Expert proficiency in scientific computing and ML tools (e.g., Python, PyTorch/TensorFlow, scikit-learn) and experience deploying analytics across varied computational environments.
Ability to interpret and communicate data-driven results within an engineering or physical sciences context to technical and non-technical audiences, including sponsors.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

Recognized expertise in energy generation, energy resources, or power systems, including reactor, thermal, geothermal, grid, or integrated energy system applications.
Experience with physics-informed machine learning, surrogate modeling, digital twins, or uncertainty quantification for complex natural or engineered systems.
Experience working with instrumented, operational, or spatially distributed data (e.g., sensor time series, plant monitoring, geospatial and remote sensing datasets, anomaly detection, predictive maintenance).
Established relationships with DOE program offices, federal sponsors, or industry partners in the energy sector.
Experience mentoring staff and leading multidisciplinary or cross-organizational research teams.
Active leadership in professional societies and service on technical review panels or editorial boards.
PhD in an engineering, physical sciences, or earth sciences discipline (e.g., nuclear, mechanical, chemical, or electrical engineering; physics; geosciences; applied mathematics).

Physical Requirements

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel, bend, use hands to handle materials, manipulate tools, keyboard and type, reach with hands and arms, and operate job related equipment. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Sufficient visual acuity and hearing capacity to perform the essential functions and interact with people is required. new_jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Computer Vision
new_jobs.description:
About Mecka AI

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

The role

Mecka captures how people move, work and interact with the physical world. The footage is messy: hands disappear behind objects, cameras turn quickly, and motion blur hides the details. You’ll build models that make sense of it—and turn it into accurate 3D data that robotics teams can train on.

We’re looking for machine learning engineers with depth in pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction who want to own what happens after the experiment works. You’ll train models, investigate where they fail and get them running reliably in production, working across the perception stack along the way.

What you’ll do

Build models for the problems in front of us. You’ll train vision models from scratch on large multi-view, multi-sensor datasets, developing new losses and architectures where existing methods fall short.
Work through the difficult footage. You’ll tackle motion blur, fast rotation, heavy occlusion and partial views of hands, bodies and objects.
Find out where your models fail. You’ll evaluate them on our own video, measuring real error and failure rates alongside public benchmark results.
Own the path to production. You’ll optimize GPU performance, make results reproducible, integrate models into our data pipeline and ship releases you can roll back.
Follow problems through to a fix. You’ll reproduce customer-reported issues, understand what went wrong and deliver a fix. You’ll also prototype quickly as new perception problems come up.

What you’ll bring

Strong machine learning fundamentals. You’re comfortable building and training models with Python and PyTorch.
Experience training large vision models from scratch. Your experience goes beyond running or fine-tuning existing models.
Depth in a computer vision specialty. You’ve worked deeply in at least one area, such as pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction.
Experience owning models in production. You’ve shipped a model or perception component and stayed responsible for it afterward.
Comfort with the work as it is. You can make progress with noisy real-world data and adapt when priorities shift.

Nice to have

Experience in one or more of these areas would be valuable:

Hand and body tracking: 3D hand and full-body tracking, mesh recovery, human-object and human-scene interaction, and estimating contact with objects and the ground.
SLAM, VIO and calibration: Learned ego-motion, optical flow, online calibration and metric scale.
3D reconstruction and objects: Feed-forward or per-scene reconstruction, Gaussian splatting or NeRF, and neural 3D object estimation from egocentric video.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, we will partner with you to meet your needs.

We may use AI-assisted tools to help evaluate applications against the requirements of this role. These tools support our recruiting team in identifying qualified candidates but do not replace human judgment or limit which applications may be reviewed or considered.
